gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold defect is failure of the displayed Brownian-bridge control to belong to the stated space-time L2 admissible class because its stochastic-integral second moment diverges. ISSUE-002 concerns division by zero in a discretized algorithm at the terminal grid step; it does not diagnose the control's admissibility or the invalid exact-equivalence argument.

The gold defect is an incorrect pointwise/almost-sure claim for the random value V_epsilon(0,x_0), where only an expected-value estimate is supported. ISSUE-003 concerns missing regularity and growth justification for a Feynman-Kac or maximum-principle proof of a particle-approximation rate, not confusion between pointwise and expected-value bounds.

The gold defect is the incorrectly scaled completion of squares in the verification identity, yielding the wrong minimizer and feedback. ISSUE-006 concerns omission of shared non-i particle costs from a conditional Monte Carlo weight; it does not recognize the epsilon scaling error in the verification formula.

The gold defect is that an Ito calculation supports only an expected L2 contraction and cannot establish the claimed samplewise contraction or separate pointwise Lions-kernel bounds. ISSUE-003 identifies absent growth and regularity hypotheses for a different Feynman-Kac/maximum-principle step in the particle-rate proof, without recognizing this invalid contraction inference.

The gold defect is that the mean-field pseudocode uses an undefined general-functional call and fails to use one common terminal configuration and common weight for each Monte Carlo index. ISSUE-006 instead diagnoses an algebraically false simplification caused by omitting shared non-i costs; it does not recognize the undefined interface and required joint sampling construction.
